availableCommands.name: skill:hf-cli
availableCommands.description: Hugging Face Hub CLI (`hf`) for downloading, uploading, and managing models, datasets, spaces, buckets, repos, papers, jobs, and more on the Hugging Face Hub. Use when: handling authentication; managing local cache; managing Hugging Face Buckets; running or scheduling jobs on Hugging Face infrastructure; managing Hugging Face repos; discussions and pull requests; browsing models, datasets and spaces; reading, searching, or browsing academic papers; managing collections; querying datasets; configuring spaces; setting up webhooks; or deploying and managing HF Inference Endpoints. Make sure to use this skill whenever the user mentions 'hf', 'huggingface', 'Hugging Face', 'huggingface-cli', or 'hugging face cli', or wants to do anything related to the Hugging Face ecosystem and to AI and ML in general. Also use for cloud storage needs like training checkpoints, data pipelines, or agent traces. Use even if the user doesn't explicitly ask for a CLI command. Replaces the deprecated `huggingface-cli`.

availableCommands.name: skill:find-skills
availableCommands.description: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.

availableCommands.name: skill:stack-diagram
availableCommands.description: Create cloud-architecture-style diagrams of tech stacks, system architectures, infra layouts, and service topologies — with real brand logos, grouped containers, and clean orthogonal arrows — delivered as self-contained HTML, a PNG image, a React/TSX component, or a live artifact. Use this skill whenever the user asks for an architecture / system / stack / infra diagram, a tech-stack overview, a service topology, a cloud-vendor-style diagram, or wants tech logos arranged into a picture of how their services connect — in any language, even if they don't name an output format, and even if the tools involved aren't cloud services.
